s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive unilateral limb weakness with motor aphasia and an intracranial lesion
salient_findings: Abnormal CSF analysis with high cell count and protein
Lung mass with pleural invasion on chest CT
key_facts: 66-year-old man
Progressive right-sided limb weakness for 3 days
Excessive smoking history
Thyroid nodules history
No history of hypertension, diabetes, or heart disease
No headache, vomiting, unconsciousness, or seizures
Right hemiplegia (MRC 0/5) on physical examination
Cortical motor aphasia on physical examination
Elevated WBC count (14.53*10^9/L)
Elevated neutrophil count (79%)
Normal blood glucose level (5.82mmol/L)
Abnormal CSF analysis
Intracranial lesion on head MRI with severe edema and circular enhancement
Lung mass with pleural invasion on chest CT
Inflammatory cell infiltrates and fibrin-like exudates on lung biopsy
Multiple fungal hyphae identified on brain lesion pathology

s4.champion: Lung cancer with brain metastasis and fungal infection

raw.champion: Lung cancer with brain metastasis and fungal infection
raw.rationale: The patient's history of excessive smoking, presence of a lung mass with pleural invasion, and an intracranial lesion with severe edema and circular enhancement support the diagnosis of lung cancer with brain metastasis. Additionally, the identification of multiple fungal hyphae in the brain lesion pathology and inflammatory cell infiltrates in the lung biopsy suggest a concurrent fungal infection.
